quotes.quote: with Jellyfin today and whatever the open media server streaming landscape looks like in the future
quotes.excerpt: Fully open stack TV streamer, think open source Roku or AppleTV. Same for Airplay for audio. This enables open source digital sovereignty end to end for streaming media, with Jellyfin today and whatever the open media server streaming landscape looks like in the future. Hardware authenticator to wave for access based on vein print biometrics. Similar to https://github.com/ZimengXiong/TinyTouch Open source library man

threads.title: Ask HN: What self-hosted apps do you use daily?
Ask HN: What is some software that you wish existed?
Ask HN: I'm fed up with my Chromecast/Google TV. What are my options?

quotes.excerpt: * PiHole - dns * Jellyfin - videos and such * mealie - recipes * aphorio - my own app for container management, web servers, sockets, and more. It can do 5,000,000 messages person on a single socket roundtrip * gamevault - like Jellyfin for games * there is an audio app I wrote that I use daily * ghost - blogging on my public web server There are some others I run additionally but those listed above are the main ones

quotes.quote: You can run jellyfin on many TVs or maybe plex.
quotes.excerpt: This would be a rpi or mini PC plugged in, yeah. Really it's not actually much different than Chromecast, same general ideas and technologies. It might be possible to make an open screen server that runs on Android running tv's, but deploying to those things is, to my understanding, a sort of deliberate hell orchestrated by everyone involved, from Google to the TV makers. Generally I recommend -- like with Chromecast
